edition.notes: A current commentary and reconstruction informed by the Ethiopic witness published in 2011. Only the publisher-authorized introductory preview is registered and inspected; chapters 20-21 are not present in that preview.
edition.publication: Paul F. Bradshaw (Collegeville, Minnesota: Liturgical Press Academic, 2023)
edition.title: Apostolic Tradition: A New Commentary

passages.context: Preview artifact pages 15-16 were read with the surrounding introduction. Bradshaw identifies the Ethiopic E1 witness published by Alessandro Bausi in 2011 as an early direct translation from Greek that corresponds closely to the Latin for a significant portion, while the other oriental versions reflect a different and already expanded textual tradition. This verifies a reconstruction-history claim only; the preview does not control wording in chapters 20-21.
passages.notes: No copyrighted text is transcribed. Full versional collation and the commentary on chapters 20-21 remain open pending lawful access to the complete edition.

work.description: An early church-order text reconstructed from fragmentary and versional witnesses. Attribution to Hippolytus, unity, date, and Roman provenance remain disputed; this neutral work identity does not resolve those questions.
work.title: Apostolic Tradition
